physicalrailways.ponder.shared.bogey_pla: Right-click suitable track with a Physical Bogey to place it. With Blocks & Bogies installed, sneak-right-click for style selection and match the track gauge
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.bogey_phy: Placement creates a physical bogey immediately; no assembly at the controls is needed
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.bogey_bui: Build on the top mount and glue together the blocks that should move as one carriage; bogeys can also attach beneath an existing physical body
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.bogey_pow: Supply rotational power through the top of the mount to drive the wheelset
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.bogey_dri: Input RPM determines the available target speed; load affects stress demand and acceleration
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.bogey_rer: R-Click with a Wrench to toggle brakes; when off track, stop, select the carriage with the Wrench, then R-Click a target track with enough room
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.bogey_rem: Sneak-R-Click with a Wrench to remove the entire bogey; an ordinary R-Click does not remove it
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.controls_: Place the controls on a physical carriage; only the first-placed controls in a consist manage power for the whole train
Aim directly at the handle or red button. No driving mode is required; movement and looking remain normal
Aim at the handle, hold right-click and drag or scroll to change traction and brake notches; release to keep the notch

Right-click the selector left or right to preselect the next junction; the center cancels. Directions follow travel. It centers after the leader locks a new branch; following carriages keep that route
Right-click the red button to apply emergency braking immediately
Once stopped, hold right-click on the red button for about one second to reset emergency braking, then set the handle again
Sneak-R-Click to open settings and change the train name or each traction notch's target speed
R-Click the controls with a Schedule to store it and start running it; insert it while stopped and provide power for departure
Looking at the controls leaves automatic operation running. Holding the handle pauses the Schedule; resume it in settings
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.transfer_: Use a Rail Docking Connector on both the carriage and the world; face them toward each other and align them at the stopping position
R-Click the world connector with a Wrench to select it first
Then R-Click the destination station with the Wrench to bind it; selecting and clicking the same station again unlinks it
Associate a mailbox with this station and set its address; the connector reads the station's mailbox addresses rather than replacing the mailbox
Run a Fetch or Deliver Packages Schedule from the controls; the train must stop at the bound station before automatic docking is requested
Wait for both ends to pair and lock; packages are then exchanged according to task direction and matching addresses
Connect carriage storage to the connector with real funnels, chutes or other transfer devices; it does not remotely access every chest on the train
R-Click a connector with an empty hand to inspect its linked station, mailbox addresses and docking status
After the task finishes, docking is released before departure; external redstone power must also be removed to allow release
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.electric_: Install an Electro Energetics pantograph and physical train controls on the carriage; disconnect rotational input at the mount when testing electric-only traction
Place catenary holders above the track, then R-Click them in sequence with a wire spool to connect the overhead line
Connect the catenary to a DC supply circuit and a Ground Rod; supply voltage must meet the train minimum configured in Electro Energetics
R-Click the pantograph with an empty hand to raise or lower it; it must contact an energized overhead line, and being raised alone does not mean power is available
With an empty hand, aim at the handle and hold right-click to operate it. Manual operation pauses the automatic Schedule
Aim at the handle, hold right-click and move into traction. Actually received electrical power is shared by the consist’s powered bogeys under the controls’ command
A traction notch sets a target speed; voltage, available power and load still limit acceleration, so full traction does not guarantee reaching the target
Lowering the pantograph or leaving energized catenary removes electric traction; if the train will not move, check contact, voltage, brakes and traction notch
Braking remains available without electrical supply. Right-click the red button to stop; once stopped, hold it for about one second to reset

gui.physicalrailways.driver.pause_first: Pause the Schedule before changing direction
gui.physicalrailways.driver.route_automa: The Schedule controls automatic routing; manual preselection is unavailable
block.physicalrailways.driver_console.to: Left and right preselect a branch; the center cancels. The selector centers after the leader locks a new junction
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.couple_in: Install matching couplers facing each other on separate physics bodies. Touching carriages alone does not form a consist
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.couple_se: Stop and bring the carriages close, then right-click both unconnected endpoints in order with the Coupling Tool
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.couple_gr: A coupled consist shares its oldest valid controls. Carriages remain separate bodies that can turn relative to one another
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.couple_fo: Powered bogeys share traction; unpowered carriages are towed. Controlled bogeys brake together and followers keep the leader’s locked branch
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.couple_un: Right-click a connected endpoint with the tool to uncouple. Stop and secure the carriages first
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.couple_li: Different coupling mechanisms cannot be mixed arbitrarily. Supported trackside couplers retain their own operating rules
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.settings_: Sneak-right-click the controls to open settings. Viewing settings does not pause automatic operation
Choose forward or reverse in settings. Stop, remove traction and pause the Schedule before reversing
Edit and apply P1–P8 target speeds on the notch page. Targets must not decrease; RPM, power and load still limit actual speed
Edit the train name in controls settings; leave it blank for the default. Ownership display comes from the placement record
Engineer’s Goggles show binding, direction, notch and status. Sneak for more journey, destination, distance and speed information
With a Schedule installed and the train stopped, adjust junction priority in settings. Priority cannot bypass occupied sections or replace signals
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.schedule_: Place and name Create stations on connected tracks in one dimension. Build the physics train with its bogeys; do not assemble it at a station
Edit destinations and waits in a Create Schedule. With the train stopped, right-click the controls with it to install and start
Use settings to pause or resume; stop before skipping, restarting or retrieving the Schedule
Supported instructions cover station destinations, speed, journey titles, fetching and delivering packages. Package tasks also need railway docking facilities
Holding the handle for manual operation pauses the Schedule. Releasing keeps the notch; resume the task explicitly in settings
After rejoining, automatic work waits for the saved consist to recover. Check loading, couplings and bogeys if members are missing
A station stop is confirmed from the actual stopped position. Stations do not assemble, disassemble or exchange this train’s Schedule; dimension travel is unsupported
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.wait_time: Use delay and time-of-day waits, arranged using Create’s condition groups
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.wait_reds: Station power, Redstone Link and station-unloaded waits are supported. Unloaded waits do not force station chunks to load
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.wait_carg: Item and fluid thresholds inspect recognized onboard storage across the consist. Counting storage does not connect its inventories
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.wait_idle: Cargo inactivity waits observe real transfer activity. Keep the actual connector-to-container handling route available
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.wait_pass: Passenger waits count living, non-spectator players actually seated in Create seats. Standing players, animals and other seat types do not count
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.wait_resu: Check controls status when stations, power, consist members or connections are missing. Unknown or unavailable observations do not count as completed conditions
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.network_s: For manual driving, right-click the selector left or right for the next junction; the center cancels. Left and right follow actual travel
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.network_c: The selector centers only after the leader commits a new junction. Preview and signal waiting do not consume it; followers keep the committed branch
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.network_a: Automatic routing follows the Schedule and disables manual preselection. A new click cannot rewrite the branch under a consist still crossing
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.network_s: Automatic driving stops for normal and chain signals and resumes when permitted. Manual driving reports occupancy but does not enforce a stop for the driver
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.network_o: Train observers support train identity and item/fluid filters. Unavailable cargo information is not reported as a match
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.network_d: Use native Display Links for train, destination and arrival information. Later arrivals may be pending; wildcard matches are not a promise to stop at every station
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.network_r: Native train interfaces provide query views; edit the name in the controls. Optional Xaero integration shows a consist marker without spawning radar entities
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.cargo_sto: Chests and tanks are real onboard blocks. Sharing a body or a coupled consist does not connect separate storage
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.cargo_pat: Connect storage to the real handling endpoint with funnels, belts, pipes or the supported mod’s explicit connections
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.cargo_sco: Controls and observers can summarize consist cargo, but that query is read-only; it is not remote access to every chest
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.cargo_con: Hose, Simulated and Automated Logistics connectors retain their native transfer and explicit selection rules. Native Portable Storage Interfaces do not directly handle these physics containers
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.cargo_pac: Automatic package work uses Railway Docking Connectors and station-linked mailboxes. Onboard packages must move through real handling paths to and from the buffers
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.cargo_blo: Check full buffers, address mismatches, disconnected facilities and external redstone locks. Waiting never makes undelivered packages disappear
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.variant_s: With Blocks & Bogies installed, sneak-right-click while holding a Physical Bogey to open style selection. Available styles depend on installed compatible mods
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.variant_g: Steam ’n’ Rails integration adds supported broad, narrow and monorail styles. Match the bogey style and size to the target track
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.variant_m: A body can use multiple bogeys. Keep the wheel body separate when gluing; the mount connects the body and accepts rotational input
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.variant_p: A bogey can run from rotational input. Installed controls coordinate traction and braking; actual power and load still limit target speed
physicalrailways.ponder.shared.variant_l: After loading, check mount brakes, couplings and guidance. If derailed, stop, select rerailing with the wrench and choose suitable track
